previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with bloody mucus per rectum and melena from her ileostomy following her third cycle of R-ICE chemotherapy for EBV-positive classical Hodgkin lymphoma. She was found to have C. difficile infection causing colitis, confirmed by stool testing and supported by endoscopic findings. She was treated with oral vancomycin and metronidazole, with resolution of symptoms. Her neutropenia and anemia were managed with filgrastim and red cell transfusions. Hyperglycemia, worsened by IVIG and steroid effects, required insulin initiation and dietary modification. Mucositis and chronic back pain were managed symptomatically. She remained stable, with improving lab values, and was discharged home on oral vancomycin to continue until readmission for stem cell transplant. Pre-transplant evaluations, including MRI and dental clearance, were completed, confirming suitability for transplant.
